## Existing functionality to preserve

The two original requested features already have local implementation and audit coverage: durable application/company history and opening the top five eligible unopened jobs from the complete filtered/sorted result. They remain release regressions, not duplicate greenfield feature tickets.

- `JobTrack` represents application history. `CsvRow.clicked` represents visiting a link. Their IDs belong to different tables; a track ID is never a row ID.
- Application/company history must survive reload, logout/login and deletion of source CSV rows. Source deletion detaches references rather than deleting application memory.
- Batch opening must apply the full server query and stable sort, including results outside the visible page. Select at most five valid unopened HTTP(S) URLs.
- Reserve popup tabs synchronously during the click, close unused blanks, isolate `window.opener`, and record a visit only for tabs successfully navigated. A blocked popup must not mark a job visited.
- A website opens tabs in its current browser; it cannot force another installed browser such as Google Chrome. Provide clear popup permission guidance and preserve a manual fallback.
- Existing company history, pipeline, sessions, analytics, saved views, imports and ApplyPilot behavior must be regression-tested where a shared writer/query changes.

<a id="shared-contracts"></a>
## Shared contract conventions

**Stack and ownership.** Keep FastAPI, synchronous SQLAlchemy and React/Vite. Use the current `get_current_user`/`get_db` patterns. Every private lookup and mutation filters by authenticated user before operating. Client-supplied `user_id`, backup IDs, canonical hashes, UUIDs and integer IDs never confer ownership. Return404 for inaccessible owned entities; do not reveal whether they exist for someone else.

**Current names versus proposed names.** Existing persisted CSV columns and public query names stay compatible. New logical names in the group contracts define proposed DTOs. The verified ORM bindings are JobTrack.url for the existing application URL and JobTrack.follow_up_at for its follow-up timestamp. Preserve existing wire spelling through explicit DTO adapters. JobTrack.session_id is Text, not a declared SearchSession foreign key. Existing JobTrack timestamp columns use DateTime without timezone=True; explicitly normalize their UTC convention at the boundary and test legacy values before any timezone-storage migration. Existing status enumeration remains authoritative unless an explicit migration ticket changes it. Date/time fields are UTC instants internally; account IANA timezone controls day boundaries and display.

**Transactions and retry identity.** Validate before write. A mutation and its required history/idempotency record commit together. On exception roll back the entire logical operation. A UUID request key must be stored with account, operation scope and payload hash; a repeated matching request returns the recorded result, while a reused key with different input returns409. Scope-specific tables below may implement this; do not invent an unrelated distributed queue. External SMTP/file writes require their explicitly documented reconciliation states.

**Idempotency storage before shared receipts.** Where early evidence/reminder/document routes need request replay before F8 introduces `MutationReceipt`, add a named operation-key/payload-hash/result mapping in that feature's migration with a unique owner/scope/key constraint. Describe retention and replay result. Do not assume the later F8 table exists, and do not use a process-memory map. F8 may consolidate earlier mappings only as a separately reviewed compatibility-preserving migration; consolidation is not required by this plan.

**Errors.** Preserve compatibility with current clients until R5's normalized validation envelope lands. Proposed normalized errors use `{detail:{code,fields:[{field,message}]}}`; return401 auth,404 owned entity missing,409 conflict,410 expiry,413 size,422 invalid input,429 rate limit. An HTTP200 must never conceal a failed partial operation. UI retains drafts and explains retry/reload actions without displaying a traceback.

**Limits and pagination.** Limits below are proposed initial product defaults, not measured server capacity. Enforce bytes while streaming, records before mutation and field lengths before constructing ORM objects. All list APIs are bounded, deterministically ordered and owner-scoped. Cursor tampering or malformed sort input is a validation error. Performance acceptance uses an explicit fixture and observed query/runtime numbers, not unsubstantiated latency guarantees.

**Backup evolution.** R1 repairs the current nine sections. Every later persistent feature extends the v2 schema, export, reference remapping, restore and round-trip fixture in its owning schema ticket. Add `capabilities`/section version metadata when optional sections are introduced. A consumer that cannot restore a present required section must reject it or label the restore incomplete before writing; it must not silently ignore the section. Earlier v2 files without newly optional sections remain valid. Preserve backup refs and typed relationships. Authentication identities and credentials are always excluded. Document bytes require F5's bundle; JSON alone is not a complete file backup.

**Migration discipline.** Filenames003–016 below reserve sequential proposals based on the inspected001/002 baseline. Verify Alembic revision IDs and head when starting; renumber/rebase an unshipped proposal if a new migration landed. Never edit an applied historical migration or use `create_all` as proof that migrations work. Use additive deploy-first changes and test upgrade from the previous actual revision on disposable PostgreSQL. SQLite coverage is separate; do not pretend historical JSONB migrations are portable merely because ORM tests pass.

**Scheduling and locks.** A single designated maintenance process is the initial deployment choice. DB claims/leases still guard duplicate work and make recovery testable. Account locks must work across processes (PostgreSQL advisory or a locked owner row; SQLite serialized write transaction for local mode). In-process dictionaries/mutexes alone do not meet multi-process claims. Do not hold a database transaction open across SMTP or remote HTTP; claim, commit, perform bounded work, then record outcome.

**Shared file ownership.** New backup integration, main-router registration, writer-version coverage and test fixtures are part of scope when explicitly listed. Modify only the relevant section of shared files, coordinate sequentially, and run their regression tests. When a new service package is introduced in JG-002, later services reuse it.

**Documentation location.** `docs/JOBGRID_BUILD_GUIDE.md` is a proposed future implementation guide, introduced by JG-001. This backlog describes future work. The build guide must describe only implemented behavior, configuration, testing and recovery once each ticket lands; do not copy the entire future backlog into a current-state guide.

<a id="verification-workflow"></a>
## Verification workflow and evidence format

Use synthetic users and data. Existing backend fixtures can create/drop tables and browser fixtures can reset user data. Run them only against a dedicated disposable test database/account. Never point `DATABASE_URL` at a user's real database to run this checklist. Keep test-auth disabled in production.

The commands in individual tickets assume dependencies are installed and the backend shell has its **verified disposable** database and test environment configured. Use the repository virtualenv Python if present, otherwise the configured Python environment. These commands are proposed verification steps, not evidence that the new tests already exist.

```sh
# Backend shell; first verify the target is a disposable test database.
cd /Users/mac/Documents/Projects/CSV_Website/backend
python -m pytest tests/test_api.py -q

# Migration shell against a separate disposable PostgreSQL database.
cd /Users/mac/Documents/Projects/CSV_Website/backend
python -m alembic current
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic current

# Frontend shell. Playwright starts Vite; run the isolated backend separately.
cd /Users/mac/Documents/Projects/CSV_Website/frontend
npm run test:e2e -- --project=chromium
npm run build
```

Do not run all commands blindly before the ticket creates its test file. Playwright currently uses localhost:5173 and can reuse an existing server outside CI; verify which backend/account it targets before allowing fixture resets. R7 makes CI startup/readiness and database targeting explicit. Run the narrow test per checkpoint; expand to affected suites after contract edits and full relevant suites at group acceptance. No new app tests were required merely to write this documentation.

For every ticket, record: ticket ID; exact git SHA plus relevant uncommitted diff; database engine/version and Alembic revision; command; synthetic fixture; expected/actual result; test count; failure/skip reason; artifact path. Separate statuses **locally verified**, **staging accepted**, **released**. Screenshots are supplementary; assertions and persisted values establish correctness. Do not treat no-data conditional tests, SMTP log lines or an untested migration file as passing acceptance.

<a id="r1"></a>
## R1 — Repair complete backup and restore

**Priority:** P1  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 1: one exported applied job restored as zero applications.  
**Range:** JG-001–JG-004

<a id="r1-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-BACKUP-2. Keep GET /crm/backup/export and POST /crm/backup/import. Default export remains v1 until all v2 consumers pass; accept ?version=2 for the new shape. A v2 JSON document has version:"2.0", backup_id:UUID, exported_at:UTC ISO timestamp, schema_revision:string, sections:object, counts:object, checksum_sha256:string. Checksum covers canonical JSON of sections only (UTF-8, sorted keys, compact separators); it detects accidental corruption, not authenticity.
Sections are csv_rows, url_history, job_tracks, saved_views, sessions, audit_events, applypilot_batches, column_preferences and user_goal. Each record has backup_ref:string unique within its section. Export CSV_COLUMNS plus created_at, clicked, clicked_at, archived, is_duplicate and duplicate_of_ref; tracks export every non-identity persisted field, csv_row_ref and a validated session_ref only where an actual relationship exists. Record scalar JobTrack.session_id separately because it is currently Text; do not assume it equals a SearchSession FK. The exact field inventory is asserted against ORM columns and written by JG-001. Export nullable fields explicitly; do not collapse null, empty text, false and zero.
Never export users, OAuth identities, JWTs, signing keys or server filesystem paths. The importing authenticated user owns every imported entity; ignore no ownership field silently—reject user_id in v2 input. Cross-record references use backup_ref, never source database integer IDs. New IDs are allocated and mapped inside one transaction. AuditEvent.entity_id needs an entity_type-specific reference map; retain an opaque legacy identifier only as historical metadata, not as an active link. Unknown entity types are imported as detached historical events with a warning.
POST multipart file plus mode=merge_missing (default) or verify_only; maximum 20 MiB uncompressed JSON, 20,000 records total, 20,000 characters per note and 1 MiB per jd_text. Return 200 {backup_id,mode,counts:{section:{created,skipped,conflicts}},warnings:[{code,section,backup_ref}],verified:boolean}. No values or notes in warnings. Invalid JSON/schema/checksum =>400; oversize=>413; conflicting reference graph=>409; missing auth=>401. verify_only writes nothing. Existing natural keys use account+URL, account+view_type+name; destination records win on conflict. Remap a conflicting source reference to the preserved destination key, and report it. Session/event/batch retry identity is tracked using BackupImportMap(user_id,backup_id,section,backup_ref,target_id), unique across the first four fields. v1 import supports known fields but explicitly returns incomplete_legacy_backup warnings. Do not fabricate omitted history.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Deploy additive import-map migration before route changes, then UI. Disable v2 UI/export on rollback; retain the map and restored records. Never restore over the production DB as a test. Database-level recovery continues to use scripts/backup.sh and scripts/restore.sh; prove it separately in JG-024.

### Group acceptance fixture

In a disposable account upload two jobs, visit one, mark the other applied, add notes, a saved view and session; export v2. Import into an empty second account. Compare all section counts and actual field values; log out/in, verify the company and application. Import the same backup again and verify no additional records. Change one checksum byte and verify no write occurs.

### JG-001 — Freeze and validate the complete backup v2 record schema

**Status:** COMPLETED / locally verified  
**Priority:** P1  
**Type:** verification/operations  
**Execution position:** 1/64; group step 1/4

#### Goal — what to complete

Freeze and validate the complete backup v2 record schema. The deliverable is limited to the exact scope and numbered checkpoints below; later tickets own the remaining group work.

#### Why this exists

The current export is lossy even before import, so restoring only job_tracks would leave another false recovery promise.

Audit defect 1: one exported applied job restored as zero applications.

#### When to do it and dependencies

Start after current-source intake confirms the R1 failure and the isolated test setup is safe.

Shared prerequisites: [contract conventions](#shared-contracts), [verification workflow](#verification-workflow), and [R1 group contract](#r1-contract).

#### Estimated effort and execution size

Small–medium — bounded to the numbered checkpoints and named tests. This is a relative estimate, not a delivery promise. Run the numbered checkpoints separately; if one checkpoint requires an unrelated schema or new external service, split and update this plan before expanding scope.

- [docs/TEST_AND_FEATURE_REVIEW_2026-09-12.md](../docs/TEST_AND_FEATURE_REVIEW_2026-09-12.md)
- The complete [R1 frozen proposed contract](#r1-contract), including limits, compatibility and rollback.

- [scripts/backup.sh](../scripts/backup.sh)
- [scripts/restore.sh](../scripts/restore.sh)

Use the graph to locate the current writer/query and read its real source. Verify ORM field names, route prefixes and current test fixtures before adding an adapter. The group contract is a proposed target; source verification is the intake check, not permission to change behavior silently.

#### User-facing behavior

This ticket establishes the storage, service or verification behavior used by the next ticket. It does not by itself claim that a new screen or live integration is available. Existing user workflows must continue passing.

#### Frozen source requirements

Implement the [R1 contract](#r1-contract) without changing original application-versus-visit semantics, owner scoping or complete-query filtering. Proposed design defaults may be revised only by updating this contract and its dependent tests together.

Audit defect 1: one exported applied job restored as zero applications.

#### Exact scope

- Create strict Pydantic v2 backup models with extra=forbid and an explicit section field allowlist
- List every current model column as exported, reconstructed, deliberately excluded with reason, or an unresolved migration blocker; include UrlHistory and preference/goal rows
- Define backup-local references and canonical checksum serialization; use allow_nan=False and reject duplicate JSON object keys
- Validate lengths, total-record limits, section uniqueness and reference targets before constructing ORM objects
- Implement a v1-to-internal-format adapter that records which fields were absent; never infer first application dates
- Write the v2 example and version compatibility table in the build guide

#### Step-by-step implementation — how

1. **JG-003.01 — Read at most 20 MiB plus one byte; use application body limits as a second guard and do not call unbounded file.read.**

2. **JG-003.02 — Parse and validate the entire record graph and checksum before beginning destination writes.**

3. **JG-003.03 — Build a preflight plan of creates, natural-key skips, conflicts and remapped references; verify_only returns that plan.**

4. **JG-003.04 — Insert sessions and rows before dependent tracks, batches and events; resolve duplicate_of after all source rows have mapped IDs.**

5. **JG-003.05 — Insert restored rows, preferences, goals and import identity mapping in one transaction; use savepoints or an upsert for concurrent map uniqueness.**

6. **JG-003.06 — On retry return stable mapping results without repeating mutations; on any insert/reference failure roll back every section.**

7. **JG-003.07 — Preserve destination-owned records on merge conflicts and report exact counts; v1 omissions produce explicit incomplete warnings.**

3. **Proposed regression `test_failure_on_last_section_rolls_back_all`** — assert injected constraint failure leaves zero partial rows. Use nonempty fixtures and an exact expected value/status/count; do not merely assert that a request returns a response.

4. **Proposed regression `test_merge_preserves_newer_destination`** — assert no existing note/status is overwritten. Use nonempty fixtures and an exact expected value/status/count; do not merely assert that a request returns a response.

5. **Proposed regression `test_wrong_account_and_reference_injection`** — assert no foreign IDs attached. Use nonempty fixtures and an exact expected value/status/count; do not merely assert that a request returns a response.

<a id="r2"></a>
## R2 — Make filtered exports match browsing

**Priority:** P1  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 2: remote-only list contained one row, export contained two.  
**Range:** JG-005–JG-007

<a id="r2-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-FILTERS-1. Keep existing GET /rows and export routes and snake_case wire names. Introduce immutable RowQuery input shared by list, export and batch selection: sort_by,sort_dir,ats_group,location_group,search_bucket,decision,sponsorship_status,fit_category,seniority_level,work_model,role_family,salary_min,salary_max,q,opened_only,unopened_only,has_error,jd_missing,openable_only. Preserve current parameter defaults and sort validation; q max 500; booleans explicit. Pagination belongs to list only and is never reused to limit a filtered export. Stable secondary order is CsvRow.id descending after the chosen primary sort; nulls last. Both opened_only and unopened_only produce zero matches for old clients, while UI prevents setting both.
An ApplicationQuery contains all currently supported filtered_query arguments including quick_range,date_from,date_to,min_score,max_score,follow_up_due,opened_not_applied,date_applied_from,date_applied_to,applied_only and the additional follow-up and row-derived filters. Inventory their exact names before extraction; preserve existing camelCase-to-snake_case client mapping until migrated together.
GET /crm/export/dashboard accepts RowQuery plus format,columns,row_ids. Explicit scope=all|filtered|selected is additive; omitted scope retains legacy behavior. selected requires a nonempty valid list of at most 500 account-owned IDs and excludes archived rows unless explicitly requested by the later archive feature. Reject malformed/empty row_ids, never fall back to all. CSV cells beginning =,+,-,@ or control whitespace followed by a formula marker are prefixed with a single quote in spreadsheet-safe mode (default), with lossless JSON offered separately. Do not mutate stored values. Invalid filters=>422; unknown sort/column=>400; missing/foreign selected IDs=>404. Existing envelope and download filenames remain compatible.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Deploy server accepting additive parameters before the new client. Roll back callers and query helper as a unit if ID parity fails; no schema change. Keep explicit export tests to prevent silently expanding scope.

### Group acceptance fixture

Upload 61 matching jobs plus two controls; set ATS, remote, sponsorship and search filters, sort title ascending, navigate to page 2, then export filtered JSON. Compare its complete ordered IDs/URLs against all pages of GET /rows with the same query. Export two selected IDs and confirm exactly those two are present.

<a id="r3"></a>
## R3 — Reconcile visits applications and progress metrics

**Priority:** P1  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 3: applied_today=1 but goal applied=0; one visit but weekly opened=0.  
**Range:** JG-008–JG-011

<a id="r3-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-LIFECYCLE-1. Distinguish visited (a successful app-directed navigation recorded by the user browser), saved (JobTrack exists), applied (first applied_at exists), and current status. A visit does not create an application or prove submission. Time-window metrics use first occurred_at, not mutation updated_at. Application status transitions can move backward; the first applied_at is preserved unless the user explicitly corrects the date.
Add JobLifecycleEvent: id Integer PK, user_id FK users nonnull indexed, event_key String(160) nonnull unique with user_id, job_url Text nonnull, csv_row_id nullable FK SET NULL, job_track_id nullable FK SET NULL, kind String(32) nonnull, occurred_at DateTime UTC nonnull, recorded_at DateTime UTC nonnull, source String(32) nonnull, payload JSON nonnull default {}. Kinds: first_visited,first_applied,status_changed,applied_date_corrected,followup_changed; payload uses a per-kind allowlist, never full notes or resume data. Retain job_url as private domain data in DB, never logs. Event keys for first events derive from sha256(account+exact job URL+kind); transition keys are caller operation UUIDs.
Add User.timezone String(64) nonnull default UTC (legacy migration default only); API GET/PATCH /crm/profile/timezone accepts {timezone:IANA string}. UI suggests detected zone but user chooses; validate with zoneinfo.ZoneInfo. Compute [local midnight, next local midnight) converted to UTC, preserving DST day length. GET /crm/analytics, /crm/analytics/goals, /crm/analytics/weekly and existing stats keep response keys but use common lifecycle service definitions. Legacy backfill only emits first events where clicked_at/applied_at is known; absence is unknown, never now. Non-date legacy status=applied produces a reconciliation warning, not an invented date.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Add event/timezone schema first. Backfill in bounded idempotent batches, compare old/new definitions before switching read paths. On rollback retain events and timezone column; old readers can run with columns present. Never delete observed history to make totals match.

### Group acceptance fixture

Set Asia/Kolkata, visit a job and save/apply a different job. Confirm visited=1,saved=1,applied=1 where shown and daily goal applied=1. Retry each mutation and verify totals unchanged. Test synthetic events on each side of local midnight and DST boundaries for America/New_York.

**Status:** PROPOSED / unchecked

#### Goal — what to complete

Wire every mutation into the lifecycle ledger. The deliverable is limited to the exact scope and numbered checkpoints below; later tickets own the remaining group work.

#### Why this exists

A ledger is useless if one path records events and another silently skips them.

Audit defect 3: applied_today=1 but goal applied=0; one visit but weekly opened=0.

<a id="r4"></a>
## R4 — Repair cleanup without enabling silent data loss

**Priority:** P2  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 4: CsvRow.updated_at is absent and the intended two-day cleanup policy is unsafe.  
**Range:** JG-012–JG-014

<a id="r4-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-RETENTION-1. Disable automatic archive and purge by default: AUTO_ARCHIVE_AFTER_DAYS=0 and AUTO_PURGE_AFTER_DAYS=0. Deprecate DELETE_AFTER_DAYS rather than mapping its value silently to destructive behavior. Add CsvRow.archived_at nullable UTC DateTime and User.retention_days nullable Integer; 0/null means no automatic archive. Existing archived=true records receive no fabricated timestamp; they remain recoverable and are ineligible for timed purge.
Explicit archive sets archived=true and archived_at=now only on the first transition; repeated archive does not reset the clock. Restore later clears both. Automatic archive may target only visited rows older than the configured period and must exclude jobs with active manual next actions or upcoming follow-ups when those features exist. The initial cleanup repair does not hard-delete anything. Permanent purge remains gated behind JG-064 and an explicit operator enablement after the recoverable archive UI exists.
Cleanup result is {scanned,archived,skipped,failed,duration_ms}; failure is distinguishable from success with zero work. Process at most 500 records per transaction, with stable ID pagination and a non-overlapping job lock. Keep scheduling in APScheduler initially; only one designated process registers maintenance jobs using RUN_MAINTENANCE_JOBS=false by default in generic web workers.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Add archived_at before updating writers; deploy no-purge cleanup with flags disabled. Roll back job activation first; retain archive timestamps. Do not downgrade populated retention columns without exporting their values. Never reinterpret old archived records as old enough to delete.

### Group acceptance fixture

Create an unvisited old row, a visited eligible row and a recently visited row in a disposable DB. With defaults no row changes. Enable a 30-day archive policy in test config: only the eligible visited row archives. Run twice; counts and first archive timestamp remain stable. Inject DB failure and verify an error signal.

<a id="r5"></a>
## R5 — Unify status date and import validation

**Priority:** P2  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 5: arbitrary status was persisted; malformed dates and malformed backup JSON returned 500.  
**Range:** JG-015–JG-017

<a id="r5-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-VALIDATION-1. Central Status is opened,applied,follow_up,interview,rejected,offer,not_applying. PATCH status may be omitted but cannot be null. Timestamp inputs may be omitted (unchanged), null/empty string (clear where permitted), or ISO-8601 with offset; a date-only string means local midnight in stored user timezone, converted to UTC. Reject impossible dates and unrecognized formats before mutation. Explicitly clearing applied_at while status remains applied is invalid 422; the UI must ask for a non-applied correction status or keep the date. Notes max 20,000 characters, company/title max 300, URL max 2048 HTTP(S), no credentials. Bulk IDs contain 1..500 positive integers, duplicates normalized, foreign/missing ID causes 404 before any write.
New normalized error detail is {code:string,fields:[{field,message}]}; preserve existing clients accepting string detail through a compatibility formatter. Do not echo raw request bodies. Invalid JSON=>400, field validation=>422, conflict=>409, not found/foreign=>404, oversized input=>413. Existing from-rows status validation is reused rather than duplicated. External import validates every record before writing; partial import becomes an explicitly different future preview/commit mode rather than accidental partial success.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Deploy compatible error rendering before enforcing new validation. Identify legacy invalid rows with an aggregate report and review them; do not rewrite statuses or fabricate dates in a schema migration. Roll back validators only if required for compatibility, retaining stored correct values.

### Group acceptance fixture

Try an invalid status, impossible date and overlong note through API and UI; all are rejected without a write. Update company only and verify dates remain unchanged. Correct an applied date deliberately and verify the lifecycle correction event. Import a two-row file with the second invalid and verify zero new records.

<a id="r6"></a>
## R6 — Make local numeric sorting and schema validation honest

**Priority:** P2  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 6: score sorting returns 500 on SQLite; Alembic uses PostgreSQL JSONB.  
**Range:** JG-018–JG-020

<a id="r6-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-DATABASE-1. PostgreSQL 16 is the deployment and migration acceptance database. SQLite remains supported for local functional tests with documented limitations; do not claim SQLite Alembic support by rewriting historical JSONB migrations. Numeric sorting in both functional runtimes accepts trimmed strings with percent/currency/comma/whitespace separators, optional leading sign and decimal point, rejecting all other formats to null. Valid numeric values sort numerically, invalid/empty nulls last, ties by id descending. Include resume_match_score,page_number,posted_age_days,jd_text_length; reuse for salary filters where identical semantics apply.
Implement parse_numeric_text using Decimal with finite-value check, then a registered deterministic SQLite SQL function jobgrid_numeric(value); registration must occur on each engine connection including test-created engines. PostgreSQL expression uses bounded regexp validation and numeric cast, not lexicographic text ordering. Do not coerce invalid values to zero. Add a fresh-PostgreSQL migration test that upgrades to head, compares actual schema with ORM expectations and exercises representative requests. Historical migrations remain immutable.

### Group release and rollback boundary

No data rewrite is needed for functional sorting. Deploy connection registration and SQL-expression selection together. For schema tests, use a disposable PostgreSQL instance; never downgrade production for a test. Record SQLite migration incompatibility explicitly.

### Group acceptance fixture

Create scores 2,10,85%,1,000,$99.50,-3,blank and invalid. Sort ascending and descending in each supported runtime; assert numeric order and nulls last. Start PostgreSQL from an empty database, migrate to head, and compare columns/indexes/constraints, not only migration source strings.

<a id="r7"></a>
## R7 — Repair CI and establish the production release gate

**Priority:** P1 release gate  
**Evidence / reason:** Audit defect 7: repository-root CI step runs cd ../backend; deployment integrations were not verified.  
**Range:** JG-021–JG-024

<a id="r7-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-RELEASE-1. CI starts backend from ${github.workspace}/backend, executes migrations on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 DB, waits up to 60 seconds with 1-second health polling, and fails if readiness never succeeds. Keep local/unit and PostgreSQL integration results distinct. Required check names are read from the final workflow; configuring remote branch protection is a separately authorized repository action, not part of writing this document.
Production startup (ENVIRONMENT=production) rejects TEST_AUTH=true, empty/default SECRET_KEY, and non-HTTPS public FRONTEND_URL/OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE. Require a signing secret of at least 32 random bytes in deployment configuration; do not test strength by logging it. Cookie security options remain server-controlled. Development/test explicitly retain local dev-login. Reject configurations before opening background workers or serving routes.
Artifact evidence per release includes commit SHA, dependency lock state, migration revision, commands/results, real OAuth provider result, SMTP sandbox delivery result, DB restore comparison and rollback notes. No external messages, production rollout, protection updates or paid resources are authorized by this planning file. Manual provider gates can remain blocked with a named owner and exact missing credential/resource; they cannot be replaced by fabricated success.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Change CI independently of application data. Deploy startup validation with configuration inventory first to avoid an accidental outage. For releases: backup, migrate additively, deploy backend, deploy frontend, smoke, then enable optional jobs. Disable jobs and roll back app before contemplating schema rollback; retained user data is the priority.

### Group acceptance fixture

Run CI from a standard checkout, confirm backend health and the full browser/pytest jobs. Exercise production config validation in subprocess tests. Restore a synthetic PostgreSQL backup into a second DB and compare retained applications; run one configured OAuth login and one authorized SMTP sandbox delivery in staging.

5. **JG-021.05 — Keep browser auth setup as a dependency and verify test collection is nonempty.**

6. **JG-021.06 — Attach test and trace artifacts on failure with retention appropriate for synthetic data.**

<a id="f1"></a>
## F1 — Today queue: the next useful action

**Priority:** Feature rank 1  
**Evidence / reason:** Reduce decision overhead after the reliability gates; existing goals and follow-up fields are inputs, not a complete work queue.  
**Range:** JG-025–JG-028

<a id="f1-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-TODAY-1. Add WorkItem(id,user_id,track_id nullable,description varchar500,due_at nullable UTC,priority smallint default1,state pending|done,version integer default1,created_at,updated_at,completed_at nullable) for manual actions only; FK track uses SET NULL. Add WorkItemOverride(user_id,action_key,snoozed_until,version), unique(user_id,action_key). Existing follow-ups stay derived from JobTrack.follow_up_at and its current state; never copy them into another mutable task table. Derived action_key is followup:{track_id}:{UTC due timestamp}; manual key is manual:{id}. The server generates and validates these keys; do not accept keys pointing to another account. Follow-up revisions generate new keys, making old snoozes irrelevant.
GET /crm/today?cursor=&limit=50&include_snoozed=false returns {items,next_cursor,as_of,timezone,counts}; cap limit100. Include overdue/due-today follow-ups and pending manual actions due before the next local midnight; undated manual actions appear after dated ones. Terminal application states are excluded using the current status enum. Sort due_at ascending nulls last, priority descending, type then ID; signed/validated opaque cursor carries the ordering tuple and as_of. No claim of an immutable snapshot across edits. POST /crm/work-items returns201; PATCH /crm/work-items/{id} requires version and returns409 on stale write. POST /crm/today/snooze accepts action_key,until (future within365 days),version. Completion of a manual task writes state=done. Completing a follow-up requires explicit resolution of its underlying follow-up date (clear or reschedule), emits followup_changed, and does not mark the job applied. Default view is read-only until an explicit action. Deadline/interview sources are added only in their later feature groups.
Shortlist/saved-view entry is deliberate: WorkItem additionally has row_id and source_view_id nullable owner-validated FKs with SET NULL, plus origin_key nullable unique(user_id,origin_key). POST /crm/today/from-view accepts owned view_id,limit1..20 and a request UUID; reuses R2 complete query/sort, then creates manual actions for the first matching rows with source key view:{view_id}:row:{row_id}. Existing pending source actions are returned, not duplicated; completed items require explicit reopen. A row/application detail action can similarly add one manual action. Retain description when source disappears. Do not automatically enqueue every search result. The queue displays a saved-view origin label; future deadlines/interviews join only when F7/F8 land.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Add tables before exposing the route. Disable the Today navigation entry to roll back; retain work items and source follow-up dates. Keep original application follow-up editing usable. Backup new user-owned records and overrides through the v2 section extension policy.

### Group acceptance fixture

Create one overdue and one tomorrow follow-up, one undated manual task and one foreign-account item. Today must contain only the overdue and undated owned actions. Snooze the overdue item, reload, advance a fake clock and verify it returns. Completing it must not increment applications.

<a id="f2"></a>
## F2 — Applied-before warnings and company aliases

**Priority:** Feature rank 2  
**Evidence / reason:** Durable history already exists; the missing value is recognition before repeating an application.  
**Range:** JG-029–JG-032

<a id="f2-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-IDENTITY-1. Keep JobTrack unique(user_id,url) and preserve its original url column. A proposed DTO field named job_url maps explicitly to JobTrack.url; do not rename the persisted column. Add nullable canonical_url_hash and canonical_url on JobTrack and CsvRow with NON-UNIQUE owner/hash indexes; collisions are candidates, never automatic merges. Normalize HTTP(S) scheme/host casing, default ports and fragment; remove only utm_* and an explicit versioned allowlist (gclid,fbclid). Preserve path casing, trailing-slash distinction and all other query keys, duplicate values and their order unless a tested provider rule proves equivalence. Reject credentials/invalid ports; cap URL2048. Unicode domains use one tested IDNA policy. Provider job IDs are strong hints only when provider and company scope are both known.
CompanyAlias(id,user_id,alias_key,display_name,company_key,created_at) unique(user_id,alias_key). Use trimmed/casefolded whitespace-normalized keys for suggestions, preserving display spelling. Explicit aliases map directly to a stable owner-local UUID company_key; no chains, fuzzy auto-merge or cross-user directory. GET /crm/application-matches?row_id= or a POST body URL for unsaved capture returns {matches:[{track_id,confidence:exact|canonical|possible,reason,company,title,status,applied_at}],company_history_count}. A visited or saved-only job is not an applied-before match; require known first applied evidence from JG-008. Company/title-only matches are possible warnings. GET/POST/DELETE /crm/company-aliases manage explicit aliases with409 for a conflicting key. Application creation returns warning candidates but never silently blocks legitimate reapplications. Canonical rules are versioned; a rule change requires dry-run collision report before backfill.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Hide match badges and alias controls to roll back. Retain original URLs and tracks, so identity helpers can be disabled without losing applications. Roll back canonical rules by rebuilding nullable derived columns, never deleting collision records.

### Group acceptance fixture

Import the same role with a utm_source variant, another requisition on the same host and an unrelated company with a similar title. The first should show canonical history, the second remain separate, and the third receive no exact warning. Add and remove an explicit company alias; underlying applications must remain intact.

<a id="f3"></a>
## F3 — Application evidence and a trustworthy timeline

**Priority:** Feature rank 3  
**Evidence / reason:** Status labels alone cannot answer when an application was made or which evidence supports that claim.  
**Range:** JG-033–JG-036

<a id="f3-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-EVIDENCE-1. Reuse JobLifecycleEvent from JG-008; do not create a competing status-history table. Add ApplicationEvidence(id,user_id,track_id,kind confirmation_url|confirmation_text|note,body text,occurred_at nullable UTC,created_at UTC,updated_at UTC,version integer,is_deleted boolean defaultfalse). Require body1..20000 for text/note, URL<=2048 HTTP(S) without credentials for confirmation_url. Evidence records are user assertions; a URL is not verified submission and is never fetched automatically. track_id must be owned and uses RESTRICT to prevent unexplained evidence loss.
GET /crm/tracks/{id}/timeline?before=&limit=50 returns chronologically ordered lifecycle and evidence events with stable type/ID tiebreaker and source label (user,import,system,legacy). POST /crm/tracks/{id}/evidence accepts Idempotency-Key UUID and returns201 (replay200). PATCH evidence requires version; writes an evidence_edited lifecycle event, never rewrites an original status event. DELETE soft-deletes evidence and appends evidence_deleted; return204, repeat204 for the same owner. Timeline carries a redacted deleted marker, not the removed body. Applied-date corrections require a reason1..500 and preserve previous/new values in the immutable event. Legacy unknown dates render Unknown; imported created_at is never presented as a submission date. Notes remain private, rendered as plain text; no HTML or automatic links from arbitrary text.
For an accidental latest status change, POST /crm/tracks/{id}/status-corrections accepts {expected_event_id,restore_status,reason}. Under a track lock require expected_event_id to be the latest status event and its recorded current state to match; otherwise409. The requested restored status must equal that event's prior valid state. Append a compensating status_changed event with correction_of and reason; never delete the original event. First-applied history remains first-applied; if the original application itself was recorded by mistake, require a separate explicit applied-date/evidence correction rather than silently erasing history. This individual correction is available before the later bulk Undo feature.
EvidenceCreateReceipt(user_id,request_key UUID,payload_hash,evidence_id,created_at), unique(user_id,request_key), is created in migration009 and retained30 days; a replay uses the stored evidence/result and never emits another lifecycle event. Soft-deleting evidence removes body from ordinary APIs immediately. Retain the original body at most30 days for the explicitly documented recovery window, then blank it through bounded maintenance while keeping a deletion marker. Account data exports include retained private body only in an explicitly labeled recovery section; ordinary timeline export omits it. The user-facing delete copy states this retention window.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable evidence editing UI on rollback and retain all rows/events. Existing status and notes continue to work. Do not roll back by deleting the ledger. User deletion policy and backups must explicitly cover evidence and its soft-deleted body retention.

### Group acceptance fixture

Mark a synthetic job applied, add a confirmation URL, correct the applied date with a reason and reload. Timeline must show original action, evidence and correction in order. Edit then delete the evidence and verify its body is absent from the ordinary timeline while the historical marker remains.

<a id="f4"></a>
## F4 — Follow-up reminders with delivery accounting

**Priority:** Feature rank 4  
**Evidence / reason:** Existing follow-up dates and email settings need durable scheduling and visible delivery outcomes.  
**Range:** JG-037–JG-040

<a id="f4-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-REMINDERS-1. Add ReminderPreference(user_id unique,enabled false,channel in_app|email defaultin_app,local_time HH:MM default09:00,quiet_start HH:MM default21:00,quiet_end HH:MM default08:00). Use account IANA timezone. Add ReminderDelivery(id,user_id,track_id nullable,occurrence_key,channel,status pending|sending|sent|failed|unknown|cancelled,scheduled_at,lease_until nullable,attempt_count default0,next_attempt_at nullable,sent_at nullable,last_error_code nullable,version), unique(user_id,occurrence_key,channel). occurrence_key contains track ID plus canonical follow-up due timestamp and notification local date, maximum one per due item per account-local day. Follow-up changes cancel unsent old occurrences. Terminal statuses suppress future reminders.
GET/PATCH /crm/reminders/preferences is owner-only with opt-in defaultfalse; GET /crm/reminders?cursor=&limit=50 lists safe delivery summaries. A designated worker claims at most50 rows using DB leases, handles expired claims and rechecks source eligibility before delivery. Do not send from GET or frontend timers. Resolve ambiguous/nonexistent local reminder time with documented zoneinfo policy: first valid instant after a spring gap; earlier offset on fall overlap, one occurrence per local date. Quiet hours defer to the next allowed local time. Email needs verified destination from account identity, configured provider and explicit preference; never accept arbitrary recipient in delivery request.
SMTP cannot provide exactly-once delivery after an ambiguous acceptance/crash. Mark uncertain attempts unknown and require deliberate user retry with possible-duplicate warning; do not automatically retry unknown acceptance. Retry only known pre-acceptance transient failures at1,5,30 minutes, maximum3 attempts. Delivery details contain no credentials or email body. In-app unread state is independently persisted; email sent only after provider acceptance, with received-message proof in staging acceptance. Scheduling configuration never itself authorizes sending during roadmap implementation.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable reminder worker and preference controls first; pending records remain paused, not deleted. Do not reset sent/unknown states or replay the outbox after rollback. Existing manual follow-up dates and Today continue to work.

### Group acceptance fixture

Using a fake clock and test mail transport, create a due follow-up and opt in. Run two workers and confirm one claim. Simulate failure before SMTP acceptance, then ambiguous acceptance; only the first retries automatically. Change the due date and verify old unsent reminders cancel.

<a id="f5"></a>
## F5 — Resume and cover-letter versions per application

**Priority:** Feature rank 5  
**Evidence / reason:** Remember which document was used, not merely the latest file on the computer.  
**Range:** JG-041–JG-044

<a id="f5-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-DOCUMENTS-1. Add DocumentVersion(id UUID,user_id,kind resume|cover_letter,label varchar150,original_filename varchar255,media_type application/pdf|text/plain,size_bytes,sha256,storage_key private,version_number,created_at,state pending|ready|failed|deleted). Add ApplicationDocument(user_id,track_id,document_version_id,attached_at), unique(track_id,document_version_id); validate both owners. Files immutable: editing creates another version, never overwrites the bytes referenced by an application. Initial scope PDF and UTF-8 plain text only, max10 MiB/file and100 MiB/account; DOCX parsing, OCR and AI tailoring are deferred. Enforce actual streamed byte limit, media signature/UTF-8 validity and safe display filename; never use supplied filename as a filesystem path.
POST /crm/documents multipart creates201 only when DB state ready and bytes persisted; require Idempotency-Key. GET /crm/documents lists owner metadata; GET /crm/documents/{uuid}/download streams authenticated attachment with nosniff, private no-store and safe Content-Disposition. POST /crm/tracks/{id}/documents links an owned ready version; DELETE the link detaches only. DELETE document returns409 while referenced, otherwise soft-deletes and schedules bytes removal under a documented retention window. No public static mount, file preview iframe or executable content. Use configured DOCUMENT_STORAGE_DIR on a durable private volume outside frontend/public and repo; proposed local storage backend must fail readiness if deployment has only ephemeral storage. Storage adapter permits later private object storage without changing IDs.
Write bytes to a random owner-scoped staging key, validate/hash, fsync and atomic rename, then mark ready; transaction/filesystem cannot be atomic together, so record pending state and reconcile orphan/missing files with age grace1 hour. Quota reservation must serialize per account. A JSON backup includes document metadata and checksums but cannot claim complete file recovery by itself. Extend backup to an optional ZIP bundle containing backup.json plus documents/{uuid}, with manifest checksums and sizes. Bound bundle to150 MiB expanded, reject path traversal, symlinks, duplicate members and missing files; restore to staging and publish only after validation. Until bundle passes round-trip, full-backup UI must clearly report document bytes excluded.
Document version numbers are scoped to (user_id,document_family_id), where document_family_id UUID groups successive versions of the same named resume/letter; allocate next version under an account/family lock. ApplicationDocument additionally stores kind and usage used|reference. Enforce one used attachment per (track_id,kind) with a partial unique index; multiple reference attachments are allowed. Changing the recorded used version is an explicit correction with lifecycle evidence, never a content overwrite. The association records what the user says they used, not externally verified submission. DocumentCreateReceipt(user_id,request_key,payload_hash,document_id,status,created_at), unique(user_id,request_key), is introduced in migration011 and retains replay results30 days. GET /crm/documents/{id}/applications lists the owned linked applications and their existing statuses, bounded50/page; it supports outcome comparison without implying causation. Keep original file version and application link intact when a new family version uploads.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable uploads/link creation on rollback; preserve ready bytes and metadata and keep authenticated downloads when possible. Never switch to ephemeral storage as a fallback. Restore metadata and bytes from the same manifest and verify hashes before re-enabling uploads.

### Group acceptance fixture

Upload Resume v1, attach it to application A, upload v2 and attach to B. Download A after reload and compare its SHA256 to v1. A foreign account cannot fetch either UUID. Restore a bundle into an empty account and compare both file hashes and application links.

<a id="f6"></a>
## F6 — One-click capture for jobs outside CSVs

**Priority:** Feature rank 6  
**Evidence / reason:** Users should be able to save an individual job without building an import file.  
**Range:** JG-045–JG-048

<a id="f6-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-CAPTURE-1. POST /crm/jobs/capture accepts {job_url,title,company,source:manual|bookmarklet,notes?} with Idempotency-Key UUID. URL required HTTP(S)<=2048 without credentials; title/company1..300; notes<=20000. Return201 {row_id,created:true,matches:[...]} or200 for identical idempotent replay. A repeated key with a different payload=>409. Create CsvRow using the actual required CSV_COLUMNS defaults, source metadata and captured_at; do not create an applied JobTrack or count a visit merely because captured. Existing exact-URL duplicate policy is applied consistently: return existing owned row with created:false and expose prior history instead of silently duplicating. Canonical/possible matches from F2 warn but require user choice for a distinct URL.
Add CaptureRequest(user_id,request_key,payload_hash,row_id nullable,created_at), unique(user_id,request_key); retain replay keys30 days. Add CsvRow.capture_source nullable and captured_at nullable with legacy rows unchanged. Notes belong to a new bounded capture_notes field until an application is created; explicit transfer to JobTrack.notes must not overwrite existing notes. No automatic page fetch in first release. GET app /capture reads URL/title from fragment only and presents editable fields; source page title/company parsing is a suggestion, never a fact. Bookmarklet runs only when clicked, reads location.href and document.title, then opens the configured app /capture#payload=encoded JSON in the current browser. Strip fragment after reading and keep draft in sessionStorage for at most1 hour through login; do not put source URL in server query logs or analytics. Authentication return paths must stay same-origin and allowlisted. Web pages cannot force Google Chrome; explain that the bookmarklet works in the browser where invoked. Full extension and automatic ATS submission are deferred.
Capture rate limit is60 requests/account/hour, enforced under the same per-account database lock using request timestamps, counting rejected repeated payload conflicts in a bounded audit counter. Return429 plus Retry-After. Define a reusable owner-scoped request-window counter in the capture migration if CaptureRequest alone cannot account for unsuccessful attempts; do not silently omit rejected attempts from abuse limits.
RequestWindowCounter(user_id,scope,window_start UTC,count), unique(user_id,scope,window_start), is created in migration012. Capture scope uses fixed UTC hourly windows; every authenticated capture attempt increments the counter in a short committed transaction before payload processing, including invalid/conflicting attempts. Cap60, return429 with seconds until the next window, retain48 hours. Rate counters are not backup data and cannot be reset by uploading a backup. This fixed-window policy intentionally permits a boundary burst of up to120 requests; change to a sliding window only through an explicit contract revision if measured abuse warrants it.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Remove Capture navigation/bookmarklet exposure to roll back; captured rows remain ordinary rows and retain their provenance. Keep idempotency records through30 days to avoid retries duplicating captures. Never mark captures applied as migration cleanup.

### Group acceptance fixture

From an external synthetic job page invoke the bookmarklet, correct the title/company and save. Reload Dashboard and locate the row with its original source. Repeat the submit and confirm one row. Log out before capture, log in and verify draft recovery without an open redirect.

<a id="f7"></a>
## F7 — Job freshness and explicit deadlines

**Priority:** Feature rank 7  
**Evidence / reason:** Stale jobs waste effort, but network failures must not be misrepresented as closed roles.  
**Range:** JG-049–JG-052

<a id="f7-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-FRESHNESS-1. Add owner-scoped JobAvailability(id,user_id,job_url,deadline_at nullable UTC,deadline_source user|import nullable,state unknown|available|unavailable|closed,last_checked_at nullable,check_reason nullable,confirmed_closed_at nullable,version), unique(user_id,job_url). Retain availability independently of a CSV source so an application can still reference it by owned URL. A user-confirmed closed state is authoritative; a checker never reopens it. 2xx means reachable, not proof that applications are accepted; label it Link reachable. 404/410 => unavailable. 403,429,timeout,parse failures => unknown; never closed. Only explicit user confirmation sets closed in the initial release.
GET/PATCH /crm/jobs/{row_id}/availability uses owned row URL; corresponding track route supports source-less application history. PATCH requires version; deadlines are ISO timezone-aware values (date-only requires explicit local end-of-day interpretation shown in UI). POST .../check creates a bounded check request and returns202, or429 with Retry-After; max one per URL/account/hour and20/account/day. Checks are opt-in; no automatic scraping schedule at launch. Server fetch accepts HTTP(S) only, no credentials, rejects local/private/link-local/reserved IP ranges for IPv4/IPv6 and all DNS answers; revalidate every redirect, max3. Use a maintained transport supporting a pinned validated destination IP while preserving TLS hostname verification and Host; do not rely on a preflight DNS check followed by ordinary re-resolution. If no verified safe adapter exists, ship manual freshness only and leave HTTP checking disabled. No cookies/auth headers, max10 seconds total,128 KiB response,HEAD then bounded GET only if needed; respect429 Retry-After and robots/site-policy review before enabling scheduled scraping.
Today gains deadline actions with key deadline:{availability_id}:{deadline_at}; exclude user-closed jobs and completed/terminal application actions using explicit rules, while preserving unrelated manual tasks. Persist snooze through F1 overrides. Deadline edits cancel/recompute unsent F4 reminders only after source eligibility is rechecked. Archive does not mean closed. Add job availability to complete backups.
Add JobCheckRequest(id UUID,user_id,availability_id,requested_at,status pending|running|done|failed,lease_until nullable,completed_at nullable,error_code nullable), with owner/requested_at and status/lease indexes. A per-account database lock serializes rate checks and insert. Claim at most10; retain safe request metadata7 days and never raw response bodies. This durable table, not process memory, supplies multi-process limits and crash recovery. Lease expiry marks the old attempt failed and permits a new deliberate rate-limited check. Transient request rows are excluded from portable backup.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable check worker first; manual deadline/status editing and stored history remain. If URL-safety proof fails, launch manual freshness without outbound fetch rather than weakening address checks. Rollback does not rewrite closed/unknown values.

### Group acceptance fixture

Set a tomorrow deadline and see it enter Today only in its due window. Test a synthetic reachable endpoint,404,403 and timeout; verify reachable/unavailable/unknown labels. Attempt localhost,IPv6 loopback and redirect-to-private targets using a mocked transport and confirm zero unsafe requests.

<a id="f8"></a>
## F8 — Recruiter referral and interview workspace

**Priority:** Feature rank 8  
**Evidence / reason:** Applications need people and scheduled conversations without expanding into an outbound sales CRM.  
**Range:** JG-053–JG-056

<a id="f8-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-CONTACTS-1. Add Contact(id,user_id,name varchar200,email nullable varchar320,profile_url nullable varchar2048,company_display nullable varchar300,notes text max20000,version,created_at,updated_at,is_deleted false). Add ApplicationContact(user_id,track_id,contact_id,role recruiter|referrer|interviewer|other), unique(track_id,contact_id,role), enforcing both owners. Add Interview(id,user_id,track_id,contact_id nullable,starts_at UTC,ends_at UTC,timezone IANA,kind phone|video|onsite|other,meeting_url nullable,location nullable varchar500,status scheduled|completed|cancelled,notes text max20000,version,created_at,updated_at). Require ends_at>starts_at and duration<=24h; overlaps produce a warning, not a silent reschedule. Contact email is optional and syntactically validated; storing it does not authorize sending. Meeting/profile links HTTP(S), no credentials, opened by user only. Contacts soft-delete; existing interviews retain a deleted-contact marker without disclosing removed private notes.
Owner-scoped GET/POST /crm/contacts (q<=200,limit<=100); PATCH/DELETE /crm/contacts/{id}; GET/POST /crm/tracks/{id}/contacts; DELETE association by owned association identity. GET/POST /crm/tracks/{id}/interviews; PATCH /crm/interviews/{id} requires version. POST creates use Idempotency-Key UUID. GET /crm/interviews/{id}/calendar.ics produces one RFC5545 event with stable UID, incrementing sequence on edits, UTC DTSTART/DTEND and correctly escaped/folded values; omit private notes and email by default. It is a download, not calendar-account sync or invitations. No sending buttons in initial scope. Today gains interview preparation actions due before start, keyed by interview ID/start timestamp; cancelled/completed interviews excluded. In-app reminders may reuse F4; email remains separately opted in. Include contacts, links and interviews in complete backups.
Contact/interview create replay uses a shared proposed MutationReceipt(user_id,operation_key UUID,scope,payload_hash,result_entity_type,result_entity_id,created_at), unique(user_id,scope,operation_key), retained30 days; insert receipt and entity together,409 if payload hash differs. Introduce it in migration014 rather than overloading CaptureRequest. Add Interview.round_label nullable varchar100, preparation_notes max20000 and ApplicationContact.referral_source nullable varchar300 so round/preparation/referral requirements are explicit. These private fields are included in account backup but omitted from ICS by default.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable workspace routes/navigation to roll back while retaining contact/interview tables. Keep downloads authenticated. Do not delete contacts to remove a failed UI. Cancel pending interview reminders when the feature is disabled without changing sent records.

### Group acceptance fixture

Create one recruiter, link to two applications, schedule an interview in a different timezone and download ICS. Import into a disposable calendar manually and verify the instant/title. Edit time and confirm Today changes. A foreign account cannot read contact notes or download the event.

<a id="f9"></a>
## F9 — Import mapping preview and reconciliation

**Priority:** Feature rank 9  
**Evidence / reason:** Repeated CSV imports should improve the job set without silently replacing user-entered application data.  
**Range:** JG-057–JG-060

<a id="f9-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-IMPORT-1. Add ImportPreview(id UUID,user_id,source_filename,source_sha256,mapping_json,normalized_rows_json,summary_json,created_at,expires_at,status ready|committing|committed|failed,version,commit_key nullable,result_json nullable); store private payload in DB initially with10 MiB upload/2000-record cap and24h expiry. Add ImportMapping(id,user_id,name varchar100,header_fingerprint,mapping_json,version), unique(user_id,name). Header fingerprint is SHA256 of exact normalized header sequence; preserve original displayed labels and disambiguate duplicate headers by position. Upload CSV UTF-8/UTF-8-BOM only initially; reject unsupported encoding with actionable error rather than corrupted text. JSON accepts array-of-objects shape only. No spreadsheet formulas are executed.
POST /crm/imports/preview multipart file plus mapping and options returns201 {preview_id,expires_at,version,columns,rows:[bounded100-sample],counts:{create,exact_duplicate,possible_duplicate,invalid},errors:[{row,column,code}]}. Map by source column index to known CSV_COLUMNS fields; URL required, validate through common service. One target field may have one source unless an explicit documented combination rule exists; initial release has no implicit combinations. Unknown source columns are shown as unmapped and never silently claimed preserved. Saved mapping reuse requires exact header fingerprint or explicit remap.
POST /crm/imports/{uuid}/commit accepts {version,idempotency_key,mode:insert_only|update_selected,update_fields:[allowlisted CSV fields],invalid_policy:reject|skip}, with a preview summary before deliberate commit. Default insert_only,invalid_policy=reject. Never update JobTrack status/notes/applied_at or CsvRow clicked/clicked_at/archived through import. Exact URL matches may update only explicitly selected source fields; null/empty replacement requires separate replace_empty=true. Canonical/possible duplicates are skip-or-create decisions, never automatic merge. Verify preview owner, expiry, checksum/version and current destination conflicts again under account-scoped lock before a single transaction (2000 maximum);409 on changed conflict plan requires new preview. Replay returns the same result. Return exact created/updated/skipped/invalid counts and row-number reasons without sensitive full row text. No partial transaction success; after commit, database outcome wins even if response disconnects. Expired previews are purged by bounded maintenance; committed results retained30 days without raw rows. Backups include saved mappings, not transient uploaded previews.
For rejected-row download retain original column sequence and original values of invalid rows in a private rejected_rows_json field until24 hours after preview creation; cap it within the same10 MiB preview budget. GET /crm/imports/{uuid}/rejected.csv is owner-only, attachment/no-store, includes source row number and error code, and uses R2 spreadsheet-safe serialization. Valid raw rows are removed after commit; invalid originals survive only until the stated download expiry, then are purged. Return410 after expiry. The UI distinguishes a complete rejected-row file from the short on-screen error summary; do not return only row numbers when the user requests recoverable rejected data.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Keep original importer behind a clearly labeled fallback until new preview flow passes; never route a failed preview into automatic old import. Disable new commit endpoint to roll back; keep committed jobs and idempotent results. No reverse mutation without F10 conflict-aware undo.

### Group acceptance fixture

Import a file with renamed/duplicate headers, one bad URL, one exact existing URL and one changed title. Preview and map columns. Default reject must write nothing. Choose skip-invalid and update only title; user notes, application dates and visited state must remain unchanged. Retry commit and verify identical counts with no new rows.

<a id="f10"></a>
## F10 — Undo and a recoverable archive

**Priority:** Feature rank 10  
**Evidence / reason:** Bulk operations need recovery without restoring stale snapshots over newer edits.  
**Range:** JG-061–JG-064

<a id="f10-contract"></a>
### Frozen proposed group contract

Proposed CCR-UNDO-1. Add CsvRow.version and JobTrack.version integers default1; every writer (including imports, restore merge, lifecycle helpers and bulk routes) increments atomically. Add BulkAction(id UUID,user_id,kind archive_rows|update_rows|update_tracks,request_key UUID,status completed|undone|partially_undone|expired,created_at,undo_expires_at default+10minutes,result_json) unique(user_id,request_key). Add BulkActionEffect(id,action_id,entity_type,entity_id,before_json,after_version,undo_status pending|restored|conflict|missing), unique(action_id,entity_type,entity_id). Snapshots include only changed allowlisted fields and enough reference context to validate owner; max500 targets/operation and1 MiB total snapshot, reject413 before write if exceeded. Do not snapshot document bytes or secrets. Retain operation metadata30 days and remove expired private before_json after10 minutes; backups may include operation metadata, never advertise expired undo as actionable.
Bulk mutation and effects commit together. POST /crm/bulk-actions/{uuid}/undo {mode:all_or_nothing|restore_unchanged} is owner-only and idempotent. Default all_or_nothing checks every current entity version equals after_version; one conflict=>409 with zero restore. restore_unchanged explicitly restores only matching effects and reports conflicts; retries cannot undo the same effect twice. Apply restored status/date fields through lifecycle correction events, not direct ledger deletion. Expired action=>410, foreign=>404. Server UTC is authoritative for deadline; UI timer is informative only.
GET /rows?archive_scope=active|archived|all defaults active; archived list retains all ordinary filters/sorting/pagination and returns archived_at with unknown legacy dates clearly labeled. POST /rows/restore accepts owned IDs1..500 and expected versions, clears archived/archived_at without altering visits/application status. Restore failure is atomic unless user explicitly chooses conflict-aware partial mode.
Permanent deletion is a separate explicit selected-row action with preview count and confirmation, never the Undo button. Initial default remains no automatic purge. Only after restore/backup gates pass may the user opt into purge of source rows archived at least30 days, using archived_at rather than created_at and excluding unknown archive timestamps. Preserve JobTrack, URL history, evidence, availability and document associations by detaching source refs; verify every new FK. Hard deletion of application history or documents is out of this ticket scope. The rollout ticket must decide whether to keep automatic purge disabled; no deployment is authorized merely by this roadmap.

### Group release and rollback boundary

Disable bulk mutation/undo UI if version coverage is incomplete. Keep archive restore read path available; retain action records until expiry. Disable purge worker before any rollback. Never downgrade version columns or recreate deleted source rows from guessed state.

### Group acceptance fixture

Archive three rows and undo within10 minutes; all return with original visited/applied states. Repeat, edit one row in a second tab, then Undo: default must reject without changing any row. Explicit restore-unchanged may recover the other two and report one conflict. Expired undo shows410 and archived rows remain recoverable from Archive.

**Status:** PROPOSED / unchecked

#### Goal — what to complete

Implement transactional bulk changes and conflict-aware undo. The deliverable is limited to the exact scope and numbered checkpoints below; later tickets own the remaining group work.

#### Why this exists

A partially applied bulk action or stale undo can silently corrupt newer work.

Bulk operations need recovery without restoring stale snapshots over newer edits.

### JG-064 — Prove recovery and decide whether automatic purge is safe

**Status:** PROPOSED / unchecked  
**Priority:** Feature rank 10  
**Type:** verification/operations  
**Execution position:** 64/64; group step 4/4

#### Goal — what to complete

Prove recovery and decide whether automatic purge is safe. The deliverable is limited to the exact scope and numbered checkpoints below; later tickets own the remaining group work.

#### Why this exists

Deletion must be the last lifecycle step, after recovery has been demonstrated.

Bulk operations need recovery without restoring stale snapshots over newer edits.

#### When to do it and dependencies

Start after [JG-063](#jg-063) has its local deliverables and relevant tests complete. Follow the group sequence; do not activate this feature before its group acceptance ticket passes.

Shared prerequisites: [contract conventions](#shared-contracts), [verification workflow](#verification-workflow), and [F10 group contract](#f10-contract).

#### Estimated effort and execution size

Small–medium — bounded to the numbered checkpoints and named tests. This is a relative estimate, not a delivery promise. Run the numbered checkpoints separately; if one checkpoint requires an unrelated schema or new external service, split and update this plan before expanding scope.

This ticket establishes the storage, service or verification behavior used by the next ticket. It does not by itself claim that a new screen or live integration is available. Existing user workflows must continue passing.

#### Frozen source requirements

Implement the [F10 contract](#f10-contract) without changing original application-versus-visit semantics, owner scoping or complete-query filtering. Proposed design defaults may be revised only by updating this contract and its dependent tests together.

Bulk operations need recovery without restoring stale snapshots over newer edits.

<a id="final-release-checklist"></a>
## Final cross-feature release checklist

- [ ] Re-run all previously demonstrated audit failures against the final code and verify their regressions fail when the defect is deliberately reintroduced in an isolated check.
- [ ] Run complete-query top-five opening with more than one page, active filters/sort, invalid URLs, blocked popups, rapid repeat clicks and safe visit accounting. State cross-window concurrency limits explicitly.
- [ ] Prove applied/company history, events, evidence, contacts, document versions and availability survive source deletion and complete backup/restore into another account.
- [ ] Compare applications, first visits, goals, weekly analytics and Today under the same fake clock and account timezone; status corrections and bulk undo produce compensating history consistently.
- [ ] Verify every private route with another account and every changed writer with version/concurrency/retry assertions appropriate to its contract.
- [ ] Run migrations from the previous production revision on disposable PostgreSQL, then application smoke tests. Keep SQLite support evidence separate.
- [ ] Verify reminder opt-out, failure/unknown states and controlled received-email proof without replaying unknown deliveries.
- [ ] Verify storage readiness, document-bundle restore and private authenticated downloads on the actual deployment storage model.
- [ ] Keep network freshness checks and automatic purge disabled unless their own enablement gates are satisfied.
- [ ] Confirm production rejects dev authentication/default secrets and the real OAuth round trip works in the release environment.
- [ ] Record commit/revision/environment, exact commands, nonempty test counts, known limits, rollback trigger and recovery evidence in the proposed release acceptance document.
- [ ] Release only the locally and externally accepted scope; leave incomplete feature flags and external gates explicitly inactive/blocked.

## Features deliberately deferred

Automatic application submission; a full Chrome extension before capture demand is proven; mailbox-wide or LinkedIn scraping; AI-generated credentials or unsupported match percentages; new analytics pages without a decision they improve; billing/teams; microservices; document OCR and DOCX parsing; continuous scraping; automatic private-history deletion. Add these only through a new scoped proposal with a demonstrated user need.

## Product acceptance after implementation

Measure missed follow-ups, repeated applications, time to capture/record a job, the share of active applications with a known next action, and whether users can recover a mistaken bulk action. Record a baseline before claiming improvement. Interview outcomes may be correlated with document versions; this does not prove a particular resume caused an outcome. Prefer fewer reliable workflows over increasing the feature count.

## Document validation and maintenance

This backlog is the planning artifact. Its unchecked boxes describe future work. When implementation begins, update the affected ticket and current-state build guide together, retain stable local IDs, and explain any changed dependency or contract. New migration filenames, source mappings and limits must be reconciled against current code during intake.

The generated document is checked for contiguous unique ticket IDs, group counts, backward-only dependencies, required ticket sections, valid local anchors and explicit existing/new file classification. These are document checks, not application tests or release evidence.
